hook.line: Sometimes *espero que* feels too light. When you really believe things will work out, you can say so with more weight.
hook.es: Confío en que todo salga bien.
hook.en: I'm confident everything will turn out fine.

examples.es: Confío en que todo salga bien.
examples.en: I'm confident everything will turn out fine.

examples.es: Confiamos en que el negocio crezca este año.
examples.en: We're confident the business will grow this year.

examples.es: Mariana confía en que el juez escuche a la familia.
examples.en: Mariana is confident the judge will listen to the family.

examples.es: No confío en que Altamira nos deje en paz.
examples.en: I'm not confident Altamira will leave us in peace.

examples.es: ¿Confías en que la abogada nos ayude?
examples.en: Are you confident the lawyer will help us? (to a friend)

rule:
*Confiar en* means "to trust". With a person, it is simple: *Confío en ti*.

To say you are confident about something that has not happened yet, add *que* and use the "asking" ending, the same one you learned after *te recomiendo que*: *Confío en que todo salga bien*.

Two things to keep: the little word *en* stays before *que*, and the verb after it changes its ending (*sale* becomes *salga*, *crece* becomes *crezca*). It is a firmer, slightly more formal cousin of *espero que*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a hope or expectation phrase. Like other wishes, it takes the subjunctive.

options: I trust you.
I trust him.
You trust me.

readAndPick.es: Confío en que todo salga bien.
options: I'm confident everything will turn out fine.
I'm sure everything turned out fine.
I trust everyone.

readAndPick.es: Confiamos en que el negocio crezca este año.
options: We trust the business owner this year.
We're confident the business will grow this year.
We hope the business grew last year.

readAndPick.es: No confío en que Altamira nos deje en paz.
options: I'm confident Altamira will leave us in peace.
I'm not confident Altamira will leave us in peace.
I don't trust that we left Altamira in peace.

readAndPick.es: ¿Confías en que la abogada nos ayude?
options: Are you confident the lawyer will help us?
Do you trust the lawyer who helped us?
Am I confident the lawyer will help you?
Vale trusts Mariana.
Mariana trusts Vale.
Mariana is confident Vale will come.

readAndPick.es: Confío en que Hernando venga mañana.
options: I'm confident Hernando will come tomorrow.
I trust Hernando, who came yesterday.
Hernando is confident I will come tomorrow.

readAndPick.es: Confiamos en que usted nos ayude.
options: We trust that he helps us.
We're confident you will help us. (formal)
You trust that we will help.
I'm confident they will understand.
I'm confident I will understand.
They are confident I understand.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *sale* or *salga* and type the whole sentence: *Confío en que todo ___ bien.*
yourTurn.answer: Confío en que todo salga bien.
yourTurn.why: After *confío en que*, the verb takes the "asking" form: *salga*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: I trust you.
yourTurn.why: With a person, *confiar en* is just *en* plus the person.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: We're confident the business will grow this year.
yourTurn.answer: Confiamos en que el negocio crezca este año.
accept: Confiamos en que este año el negocio crezca.
yourTurn.why: *Confiamos en que*, then *crezca*, the changed form of *crece*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I'm confident Hernando will come tomorrow.
yourTurn.answer: Confío en que Hernando venga mañana.
accept: Confío en que mañana Hernando venga.
Yo confío en que Hernando venga mañana.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Confío en que Altamira nos deje en paz.* Say: I'm not confident Altamira will leave us in peace.
yourTurn.answer: No confío en que Altamira nos deje en paz.
accept: Yo no confío en que Altamira nos deje en paz.
yourTurn.why: Put *no* in front of *confío*; the rest stays the same.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: Are you confident the lawyer will help us?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Confías en que la abogada nos ayude?
accept: ¿Tú confías en que la abogada nos ayude?
yourTurn.why: *Confías* is the *tú* form, and *ayude* is the changed form of *ayuda*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Mariana is confident the judge will listen to the family.
yourTurn.answer: Mariana confía en que el juez escuche a la familia.
yourTurn.why: *Confía* for Mariana, then *en que* and the changed form *escuche*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. You are talking about something not yet true, so the verb takes the "asking" ending.
Almost. English trusts someone directly, but Spanish trusts *en* someone: *confío en ti*.

personal: Say one thing you are confident will go well this month, starting with *Confío en que*.
